newsitem.title: CANADA: Canadian wheat prices dip amid brisk competition.
newsitem.headline: Canadian wheat prices dip amid brisk competition.

text.p: Record wheat production in Argentina and aggressive Australian exports should continue to weigh on Canadian wheat prices unless harvest quality in those countries drops, a Canadian Wheat Board market analyst said.

"Sources down in Argentina are saying that they're looking at a record crop down there because for the first time ever they applied a lot of inputs and fertilizer because they were seeding back in the spring when prices were at their peak, and they increased acreage too," CWB analyst Larry Sawatzky said.
The CWB revised its benchmark No1 Canada Western Red Spring milling wheat price down C$9 a tonne on Thursday.
Values in-store Vancouver or St. Lawrence were dropped to the C$194-$C214 range from the C$203-$C223 range in October.

"Australia's looking at their second largest wheat crop on record. We've been hearing that price is almost a secondary thing to Australia right now. They're focusing more on sales and they have to basically to move their crop," Sawatzky said.
Meanwhile, importers have harvested large wheat crops and their needs from the world market are smaller.
"China's looking at a record crop this year and their imports are expected to be down 45 percent from last year," he said.
European export subsidies also weighed on prices and the U.S. may reintroduce its Export Enhancement Program, he said.
"They may be more willing to use EEP if they see a big winter wheat crop coming on stream this spring," he said.
A potentially supportive factor is harvest quality of Argentina's wheat crop, he added.
"Argentine production is typically of lower quality and that's negative for feed wheat (prices) but positive for milling wheat," Sawatzky said.
He declined to disclose the prices the CWB expects wheat to reach in the coming months.
